rationale: This is a very small C++ program (37 functions, 2321 text bytes total) dominated by constructors, destructors, and table-manipulation routines (Array/SpArray/Objec), with duplicated complete/base constructor and destructor pairs (C1/C2, D1/D2) that produce identical code, so diversity-weighted cheap passes are prioritized: SUB and SPLIT get high security/diversity weights and low cost penalties because they add strong resistance at near-zero overhead, which suits a size-constrained binary where expensive transformations would proportionally inflate the tiny 2321-byte text section; FLA is weighted strongly for security since flattening is the highest-impact control-flow defense and the largest functions (~217 bytes) are simple enough to flatten safely, but its correctness risk is kept moderate (0.4) because C++ code with destructor control flow can interact badly with dispatcher restructuring; BCF is allowed with tempered security weight but elevated size/runtime cost weights (0.65/0.6) since bogus blocks are the worst size offender and would bloat such a small binary; IBR and ICALL are retained at moderate security weights with high runtime cost weights (0.6) because indirect branching/calling carries real dispatch overhead on the hot Insert/lookup paths and moderate correctness risk around C++ vtable and member-pointer semantics; IGV is kept with low cost and risk weights since global-variable indirection (e.g., the TblType tables) is cheap, safe, and directly protects this program's most identifiable data structures.
